title: Debiasing Recommendation by Learning Identifiable Latent Confounders

problem.claim: Recommendation systems aim to predict users' feedback on items not yet exposed to them, but unmeasured variables can affect both item exposure and user feedback, creating confounding bias.

gap.claim: Existing approaches cannot guarantee identification of counterfactual feedback and may therefore produce biased predictions.

contributions.claim: The authors propose identifiable deconfounder (iDCF), which uses proxy variables such as observed user features to address the non-identification of counterfactual feedback.
iDCF is presented as a general deconfounded recommendation framework that applies proximal causal inference to infer unmeasured confounders and identify counterfactual feedback.
The framework is described as providing theoretical guarantees for identifying counterfactual feedback.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly characterize iDCF as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on various real-world and synthetic datasets.
The authors report that the proposed method is effective and robust.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommendation systems predict feedback for items users have not yet been exposed to.
Unmeasured variables may affect both exposure and feedback, producing confounding bias.
Existing methods rely on untenable assumptions or directly infer latent confounders, without guaranteeing identification of counterfactual feedback.
The proposed iDCF uses proxy variables and proximal causal inference to infer unmeasured confounders and identify counterfactual feedback with theoretical guarantees.
Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets are reported to support effectiveness and robustness.

unknowns: The specific proxy-variable conditions and causal assumptions are not provided.
The theoretical guarantees are not stated in detail.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are not provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness or robustness.
